payload.headline: Activation fell 7.33% overall (material, p=5e-6); the drop is concentrated in Microsoft-calendar workspaces (-22.25%, p=0.0), while Google (-0.42%, p=0.84) and no-calendar (+8.29%, p=0.28) workspaces are flat.

cause.does_not_prove: Does not by itself prove this caused the Microsoft-specific activation drop; must be tied to segment-specific funnel movement, shown in the next claim.

evidence.quote: New users connect their calendar before anything else, so the notetaker joins their next meeting automatically. The skip option is removed.

cause.text: Release rel_0412 ('Onboarding v2: connect calendar first'), shipped 2026-02-10, made calendar connection the mandatory first onboarding step and removed the skip option -- one day after the recent check period began (2026-02-09).

cause.does_not_prove: Does not identify the specific defect behind the first_meeting_rate_7d drop -- only that it is the earliest step moving with activation, not the connect step itself (which moved the other way).
cause.text: Within calendar_provider=microsoft, activation_rate_7d fell from 0.3937 to 0.3061 (-22.25%, p=0.0). calendar_connect_rate_1d rose from 0.3321 to 0.5315 (+60.04%, p=0.0), but first_meeting_rate_7d fell from 0.5248 to 0.4469 (-14.84%, p=0.0) -- the earliest funnel step moving in the same direction as activation.

cause.does_not_prove: No ticket explicitly names rel_0412 as the cause; the link is inferred from timing and matching mechanism, and 12 tickets is a floor on affected workspaces, not the full count.

evidence.quote: Getting "admin consent required" when I connect Outlook. Our IT team takes a week to approve new apps. Any workaround so I can use the trial meanwhile?
Every time I log in it sends me back to connect my calendar, and every time Outlook says I need approval from my admin. Pretty frustrating first experience.
Where is my recording from the Teams call at 2pm? The meeting happened but Tallybird shows nothing.

cause.text: 12 distinct Microsoft-calendar-provider workspaces filed tickets about Outlook calendar connection problems (admin-consent blocks, setup loops) between 2026-02-09 and 2026-03-01, including a report of a missing meeting recording.

payload.cheapest_test: Roll back rel_0412's mandatory calendar-connect-first flow (restore the skip option) for calendar_provider=microsoft only, and watch first_meeting_rate_7d and activation_rate_7d for that segment over the next 1-2 signup cohorts to confirm recovery toward baseline (~0.52 and ~0.39 respectively).
payload.question: Did 7-day activation change in the last few weeks, and if so why?
payload.recommendation: Scope rel_0412 so Microsoft-calendar workspaces retain a skip/fallback path instead of a hard block on admin-consent-gated calendar connect, rather than rolling back the release company-wide -- Google workspaces show no regression and actually benefited from the higher calendar_connect_rate_1d.

ruled_out.does_not_prove: Does not rule out that company size moderates severity within Microsoft (s51_plus fell furthest); only shows size alone, without Microsoft, doesn't produce a significant decline.
ruled_out.text: Company size does not independently explain the drop. Within calendar_provider=microsoft, activation fell significantly across every company_size tier (s11_50 -14.09% p=0.0177, s2_10 -23.17% p=0.0, s51_plus -27.76% p=0.0058, solo -24.92% p=5e-06). Within calendar_provider=google, no company_size tier showed a significant change (s11_50 p=0.1675, s2_10 p=0.6733, s51_plus p=0.116, solo p=0.41).

size.method: activation gap x conversion gap (activated vs not activated) x trials per week in segment x ARR per paid workspace

unknowns: Whether affected Microsoft workspaces that never filed a ticket abandoned silently (12 is a floor, not the full affected count).
Whether admin-consent friction existed before rel_0412 but was previously avoidable via skip, or is a wholly new failure mode introduced by the release.
Full extent of Teams-meeting-recording failures independent of calendar connect (t_d2c3915f52 suggests a possibly separate defect).
would_change_if: If first_meeting_rate_7d for Microsoft workspaces does not recover after the scoped rollback, the admin-consent/Teams-recording issue is likely independent of the onboarding flow change and needs a direct calendar-integration fix instead.
If Outlook admin-consent ticket volume does not decline after the fix, the root cause may sit in Microsoft's own IT-approval process rather than Tallybird's onboarding flow.

payload.hypothesis: Restoring the skip for Microsoft calendar workspaces brings their activation back to baseline.
payload.kill_trigger: Microsoft first_meeting_rate_7d not back to its week 1 to 5 level for cohorts after the rollback
